# Operations

- OPS-004 (must): Every app keeps a runbook at docs/runbook.md, started from the kit's template: a Status line (Draft or In use), a Last reviewed date, a reference section on where it runs, and one how-to guide each for deploying a release, rolling one back, checking its health, reading its telemetry, restoring its data and responding to an incident; before the app's first production deployment every placeholder is filled in and the status set to In use, and the runbook is reviewed whenever how the app is deployed, hosted or stores data changes.
- OPS-012 (must): Documentation should capture standard operating procedures and clearly define how work is done; standards should be regularly reviewed and challenged to ensure that they remain appropriate; use templates and version control to maintain consistency and keep a record of updates, and include authorship and review dates. An incident response plan should define the key roles involved in managing an incident and the responsibilities of each, and must include a communication and escalation structure and the core procedures the team will follow during detection, triage, containment and recovery; regularly test incident response processes using dry runs or chaos engineering exercises. Safe deployment practice (SDP) guidelines should provide clear instructions on how to deal with data changes according to the workload's data estate design.
